headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure from residential users to large energy users, such as data centers, by requiring Dominion Energy to allocate certain costs to customers with high electric demand.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Energy Plan Targets Utility Costs, Data Center Growth
news_summary: Virginia's new energy plan proposes requiring utilities to share fuel costs exceeding forecasts and making data centers pay for the electricity infrastructure they create. This aims to address rising power demand and ensure large electricity users bear the costs of their growth, potentially reducing the burden on other customers.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water users supplying data centers to report total water volume, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency on their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: Four Data Center Bills Await Governor's Signature
news_summary: Four bills regulating data centers, including SB 553 for water consumption reporting, are on the governor's desk amid debates over new facilities in Southwest Virginia. Senator Kannan Srinivasan stated that SB 553 will bring transparency to data center water use.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including sound profiles, and allows localities to examine impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, giving communities more control over data center development.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Delegate Joshua Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate interests.
news_headline: Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: A new Virginia law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments, including noise studies, before local approval. While it mandates studies, it does not set specific limits on noise or water usage, empowering localities with more information but not direct caps.
